Subject: Temporary triage carveout request from FinHealth (need checklist)

Hi — FinHealth has opened a support case reporting corruption in a small set of inference traces after a recent model patch. They asked us to hold a 7-day data snapshot for debugging and for us to grant a short read window to their SREs. Attaching their request (summary attached).

Questions: what approvals do we need before granting a timeboxed carveout? What minimum controls (access audit, KMS logs, retention expiry enforcement) must be in place? I'd like to keep the exposure minimal and auditable.

Thanks,
Rishi

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Temporary triage carveout request from FinHealth (need checklist)

Rishi — thanks for the heads up. Quick checklist that legal/security will expect before we consider a carveout: 

- Written justification from customer (problem statement + why own logs aren't enough) — we have that in their PDF but confirm it's scoped to affected tenant IDs.
- Explicit timebox (start/end) and automatic enforcement (no manual overrides without exec approval).
- Least-privilege access: role-based read-only, exclude PII fields where possible.
- Audit/forensics: enable session recording and KMS access logs for the window.
- Data handling procedure: who can export anything and how it must be encrypted.
- Post-window actions: deletion confirmation + an audit entry in INF-8721.

I'll attach the retention exception template we use for these requests — fill who will be granted access and the precise tenant IDs. If this is just for internal triage (no customer access), note that clearly.

Attachment: [attachment: retention_exception_template.docx]

-Neha
Security Compliance Manager

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, support@finhealth.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary triage carveout request from FinHealth (need checklist)

Looping in recommended operational guardrails from the runtime side — this is my suggested minimal policy if we proceed: 

1) Scope enforcement: only FH-889 tenant namespace + listed trace IDs. Reject any wildcard queries.
2) Access mechanism: create a one-time, auditable read role (triage_reader_FH889_20270331) with expiry. No bulk export permissions.
3) Observability: enable continuous audit stream to our SIEM and snapshot the KV cache state at t0.
4) Auto-revoke: IAM role + data snapshot must auto-delete at t0 + 72 hours; deletion recorded in INF-8721.
5) Emergency override: Marissa (as manager) + Neha must approve any extension; require written business justification and new timebox.

If Legal wants to review the wording, we can route the filled template to them. I think this minimizes blast radius and keeps the process repeatable.
